content.text:
I changed `DefaultBruteForceProtector.processLogin` to read the failure timestamp (`Time.currentTimeMillis()`) before it hands the job to the asynchronous "bruteforce" executor. It used to read the time inside the job. A job that ran late saw a clock that had already moved on, for example after the test set its time offset to 21 or 42 seconds. That made the lockout `notBefore` and the delta-time bookkeeping come out wrong, so the expected lockout event was sometimes missing. That is my best explanation of the flaky `testExceedMaxTemporaryLockouts` failure. The change is 3 added lines and 1 changed line in that one file. I haven't run `BruteForceTest` or any other test, so it's untested, and I couldn't reproduce the CI failure.

I didn't build the axiomengine graph for this task, so there's no graph feedback or dogfood-log entry.
